Fort Scourbone

50683908:
Shevaroth

The ruins of the city of Shevaroth, once one of Kyonin's most populous pre-Earthfall cities, are located on the plains southeast of the Fierani Forest. Abandoned by the elves fleeing Earthfall to Castrovel, Shevaroth fell under the dominion of the nascent demon lord Treerazer in 2633 AR,⁠ and as of 4725 AR it had not been retaken.⁠⁠⁠
51684188:
Augustana

Augustana is an Inner Sea port city in the nation of Andoran located on Aspo Bay. It is the second-largest city in the nation, and boasts one of the largest shipyards of the Inner Sea region.⁠⁠
67439118:
Flame That Binds

The Flame That Binds is a shop specializing in the sale of magical goods and services, found in the Varisian city of Kaer Maga. Located in the commercial Tarheel Promenade district, it is owned and operated by the amiable bloatmage Carthagos. The wizard specializes in the manufacture and sale of magical weapons, and loves discussing their use and construction with any warrior who might drop by. Carthagos also sells spell components and foci, which makes the "Flame" a popular place for young spellcasters to congregate. He even allows magic-users without a store of their own, to meet clients at his establishment; as long as he receives a cut of any sale.⁠
72653638:
Fort Trevalay

Fort Trevalay is the only fortress that the Chernasardo Rangers built entirely themselves. It is located in the Southern Fangwood and is constructed atop a massive stone column in the center of a spacious and deep gorge formed by the Sixjaws River. Fort Trevalay was built in 4687 AR of the same light gray stone that it stands upon and is accessible only via rope bridges. It was designed from the start to fully meet the rebels' needs. It features a training hall, war room, and forge as well as many other necessary accommodations. It is the most defensible of the Chernasardo Rangers' forts. The buildings within the fort are 10 feet high, except for the main tower which rises to a height of 45 feet. The stone curtain wall around the fort is 12 feet high and rises from the edge of the stone pillar upon which the fort is built.⁠⁠⁠
80796498:
Crouching Jackal

Located in northern Katapesh, the Crouching Jackal is a huge statue that stands nearly seventy feet tall and appears to depict a jackal, although the body looks more like that of a cat (or possibly an Osirian sphinx). The head has the upright, pointed ears of a jackal and a jackal's bushy tail.

No one knows who built the Crouching Jackal or why, though some rumours claim that if a person sleeps in front of it, they will be transformed into a jackalwere. Other theories include the Crouching Jackal being a hollow and unopened treasure vault, or a vast construct used in ancient wars as a terrifying weapon. Many also believe that it is a sister statue to the lizard-like Creeping Watcher of the Vargas Swamp. Regardless of its original purpose, the Crouching Jackal can be seen for miles around and is used as a convenient landmark by local travellers.⁠
91913618:
Bloodbrothers

Bloodbrothers is a rough-and-tumble pub in the Hospice district of Kaer Maga known for its barroom brawls, which are encouraged by the pub's proprietor and bartender Tarj Halfhand. Most of its patrons are mercenaries, criminals, and prospective gladiators, who are known to start or enjoy fights and hire themselves out to patrons with enough currency or a sufficiently compelling tale.⁠
98215048:
Falcon's Hollow

Falcon's Hollow is a town in Darkmoon Vale, in the nation of Andoran. The settlement sits only a short distance from Darkmoon Wood and is little more than a logging village, comprised almost exclusively of lumberers in the employ of the Lumber Consortium and their families. With few exceptions, the buildings and their inhabitants belong to the Consortium and totally depend on the overpriced goods delivered by the organization.⁠

It is said that in times long past dwarves settled in the surroundings of Falcon's Hollow; rumors persist that forgotten treasures of their fallen civilization yet remain to be found. Yet today it is a place for the desperate with no other place to go, for outcasts and religious zealots seeking to avoid hindrances brought on by their surroundings.⁠
98317818:
Crimson Citadel

The headquarters of the feared Red Mantis assassins, the Crimson Citadel is one of the few settlements on Mediogalti Island aside from the city of Ilizmagorti. Only the Red Mantis know its exact location and features, but there are numerous rumours about the place.⁠ This means that anyone who wishes to contact the Red Mantis must make their intentions known in the more cosmopolitan city of Ilizmagorti.⁠
104423508:
Mercerene Manor

Mercerene Manor is the residence of House Mercerene, boasting extensive courtyards and gardens, and is where the retired Pathfinder Haimon Heuff resides. Adventurers of all kinds visit the manor, captivating its old lord with passionate tales of adventure that evoke memories of bygone days.⁠
106629918:
Blackblade's

Blackblade's is a successful fighting academy where former pathfinder and mercenary Benkhal Blackblade instructs his students in combat for five pieces of silver twice a week. Novices spar in the academy's courtyards, serving as an advertisement to attract more students, while the most talented are personally trained by Benkhal inside the building. Most students do not live on the premises, with the exception of the instructors, who at the end of the week lock the doors and meet with former students for parties that last until dawn.⁠
107174298:
Sokar's Boil

Sokar's Boil is one of Osirion's two volcanoes—the other is the nearby Asuulek's Mouth. Both are located in the country's southwestern region known as the Footprints of Rovagug. Sokar's Boil (or just the Boil as it is sometimes called) is currently dormant. The last eruption took place some three thousand years ago and was extremely violent.⁠
110161358:
Fey's End

Fey's End is a mysterious pit hundreds of feet deep. How it was formed and its exact nature are a mystery, but the effects it has on any nearby fey are clear. Fey creatures are drawn to the pit, and when they reemerge, they are dark, twisted versions of themselves.⁠
114400298:
Mount Ebaios

Mount Ebaios is the largest volcano in Iblydos located on the north of the island of Nenakari. The volcano's name is used as an aphorism for a cure that comes with horrible side effects. It gets this reputation from the lava that has oozed out of it for the past thousand years that is said to come from the Iblydan underworld or some other evil realm. This lava burns and traps any creature that comes near it as if in amber, only for that creature to re-awaken some time later as an undead creature that breathes out noxious fumes.⁠
118934568:
Odde & Daughter Herbs

Odde & Daughter Herbs is a good example of the semi-organised chaos that has come to embody Old Kintargo.⁠ The shop itself has been out of business for years but has since become the informal venue for street vendors and downtrodden merchants.⁠ A local cambion vendor of dubious-quality street meats named Ryk had taken up semi-permanent residence in the building selling his strangely delicious wares most days. The building is also rumored to be haunted.⁠
121743458:
Haverston's Grange

Haverston's Grange is the most successful general store in Kaer Maga, run by businessman Jol Haverston. He is a firm believer that worldly goods are of utmost importance, hating magic because a spellcaster took his left arm, and magicians see their prices rise the more they appear to be wizards.⁠
125146168:
Inner Harbor

The Inner Harbor of Riddleport is much smaller than the main harbor, which is known as Riddleport Harbor, and is located at the Velashu River's mouth. The Inner Harbor provides access to the mills and mercantile buildings of the city.⁠

Several pollutants, such as from sewer outlets and general run-off from the city, make the water of the slow-flowing river undrinkable.⁠ The waters carry a disease known as harbor gut that any who drink the water will surely catch it.⁠

135567278:
Larrad

Larrad is a large dwarven city in the region of Five Kings Mountains. The city is built up around a cluster of temple-caverns carved out by the dwarves in ancient times during the first period after the completion of their Quest for Sky. The temple-caverns served as a place of worship for their gods and as a necropolis for their honored dead. Over the centuries, the temples grew into great complexes hosting many dwarven clerics and acolytes. At the same time, the support settlements around the temples expanded and overlapped.⁠

Larrad's necropolis is used by only the renowned members of dwarven aristocracy. The Cathedral of Magrim still maintains the tombs of the Five Kings' oldest residents, and employs necromantic magic to commune with the spirits of the ancestors. The Cathedral also supports expeditions into the ruins of Saggorak which is under threat from undead and creatures from the Darklands.⁠

After the death of Gorum in 4724 AR, the dwarven deity Grundinnar and an array of dwarven heroes battled the primordial being Otolmens over the fate of a warshard that crashed at the gates of Larrad. According to the Molthuni novel When Gods Make War, Otolmens claimed the warshard was a threat to the physics of reality and demanded that Larrad and all beings exposed to the warshard must be deleted from existence, which Grundinnar refused to allow. As Grundinnar battled Otolmens, dwarven heroes rushed to Grundinnar's aid, were slain, and were raised to serve Otolmens as celestials. However, both divine entities and nearly all of the dwarven combatants were suddenly removed from reality in a loud flash, as if neither had ever existed.⁠
136496138:
Vische

The Ustalavic settlement of Vische is located in the county of Barstoi, close to its border with Numeria.⁠⁠ The House of Solace is located in the town and there clergy of Pharasma are ordained.⁠
148498978:
Mortecant

Mortecant is a neighborhood in the southern part of the Precipice Quarter where followers of Urgathoa, seeking to be corrupted by the area's necromantic energies, move from abandoned house to abandoned house, weaving through a tangled web of people as if they were undead. Even the knights of Vigil's Hope have killed several mobs without realizing they weren't truly undead. Not all members of this community are inherently evil; some cannot move because the neighborhood's reputation would lead to their new neighbors killing them if they discovered their origins. Thus, they are trapped between the Knights of Lastwall and the wall of semi-dead mobs at their backs.⁠
154393418:
Stone of Tears

The mythical Stone of Tears was once a singular structure within a Ghol-Gani city that is now in ruins on the Dahak's Tooth island of the Shackles. The Stone of Tears lies sideways, having fallen from its ornate pedestal near the city's temple. It is said that the Stone of Tears was a cage for a beautiful nymph who long opposed the empire of Ghol-Gan and was imprisoned. Should she be released, her knowledge could reveal valuable secrets of the lost civilization.⁠
156827998:
Cawshax

Cawshax, originally Cow Shacks, is an agricultural village in the Swardlands of the Isle of Kortos. It is located south of Potter's Lake at the crossroads of the Merovan Road and the roads connecting to Castinlee and Turpin Rowe, with a locally known but obscure cow path leading directly to the road to Kerrick. Both farmers and herders use the lands around Cawshax, with barley and millet as its crops and cattle as its livestock.⁠
160544038:
Omesta

Omesta is a town in the northwestern Fierani Forest of Kyonin, inhabited primarily by treehouse-dwelling gnomes, who have been living there since before the elves' return to Golarion.⁠
172119398:
Orlov

Orlov, the former coastal capital and oldest city of Iobaria, is today but a ruin of its former glory.⁠ Located on the Lake of Mists and Veils, Orlov was founded in 753 AR by explorers from Okormirr who discovered the ancient Koloran Roads. Built on top of the ruins of a cyclopean city, Orlov grew quickly, becoming larger than Orkomirr in 764 AR, and eventually the first proper city in the nation of Njalgard.

In 905 AR, Iobar, heir of Orlov's ruler Kjell, usurped the nine koffars of Njalgard and established the nation of Iobaria, with Orlov as its capital. However, after the fall of Old Iobaria in 3150 AR, Orlov was conquered by foreign powers and their pawns. In 3212 AR, Orlov was reclaimed by three warlords, marking the start of the century-long War of Restoration. During the period of New Iobaria that followed, Antoll served as capital instead of Orlov.

During 4000 AR the city was attacked by, and repelled, an invasion by frost giants from the Ice Steppes who had pillaged their way across the nation. In 4659 AR, the "plague of boils and bone-aches" hit Franax, and that town's great shipworks moved to Orlov.

Due to the town's numerous ups and downs, its population now numbers at less than half of its former numbers, and much of the city has crumbled into ruins, with the stonemasons walling off complexes deemed too ruined to inhabit. Its scheming prince, Tzakiv Korya, dreams of re-establishing the Empire, but he lacks enough troops to fully man the city's ancient fortifications.⁠ Still, the Prince has managed to build some alliances with adventure-seekers and investors in Cheliax and the River Kingdoms.⁠

The city contains many towering structures, built by cyclopes.⁠

Sze

The town of Sze is one of the settlements scattered throughout the desolate, monster-haunted land of Shenmen.⁠ It has been ruled for centuries by a cruel ghostly governor named Chou Mingxia, whose pointless pursuit of lumber is driven by her refusal to acknowledge the fall of Lung Wa.⁠
182762388:
Citadel Enferac

Citadel Enferac is the stronghold of the Hellknight Order of the Gate. Located in the Menador Mountains, Citadel Enferac is the primary place where Hellknight signifers (spellcasters) are trained.⁠

Constructed by inhuman hands, only a small part of the fortress rises upon the slopes of Mount Nyisaid. The larger part of the citadel lies within the mountain, spread through great caverns and halls. The smoke of numerous forges and laboratories rises from the fortress like eerie pennants; and spiked towers and precarious walkways mar the higher slopes. At the top of the mountain, the iron statue of a huge Hellknight guards a gate for flying visitors. The citadel includes garrisons, training halls, armories, libraries, workshops, and fortifications. Tales also tell of a prison for terrible creatures within the citadel which resembles a pit into a black eternity.⁠

Deep within Citadel Enferac is a portal that leads to the Razor Stair, a library in Stygia, fifth level of Hell. The Order of the Gate's signifers frequently go there to consult with Mahshoka and Sister Drove, two uniilas who curate the Razor Stair. Despite decades of control, the Order of the Gate has not explored far beyond the portal due to the difficulty of navigating the Razor Stair; nevertheless, its members' sojourns have brought back many fantastic secrets and powerful weapons. Spies infiltrating Citadel Enferac have reported that this portal is no longer the only one within Mount Nyisaid, and nor is it the most terrifying.⁠
192088448:
Soggy Piper

The Soggy Piper is a tavern perched on a cliff in The Puddles, a hangout for criminals and cultists. Violent crime is commonplace there, as bodies can be disposed of by simply pushing them off the cliff into the sea. The patrons avoid eye contact, creating a moody atmosphere and while the food is fairly average, it's a good place to gather information about the district's activities.⁠
192292318:
Saucy Wench

The Saucy Wench meadhall is one of the very few of the permanent buildings in the Grand Bazaar in the Coins district of Absalom.⁠ The popular four-story edifice near the center of the bazaar serves roast meat, bread, and mead, and is well-known for its uniformed all-female waiting staff.⁠ The tavern's employees all work for owner Lady Kythes Finch, captain of the Token Guard, so unwelcome advances are often dealt with by one of the many off-duty guardsmen who number among the meadhall's patrons.⁠
199772048:
Temple of Calistria

The Temple of Calistria in Kaer Maga, while influential in the city ihas lost power due to secular leaders like Elias Sayer and Rosaline Merithane, and has less authority than in other cities where the Calistrian clergy is favored. Even so, in its vengeful aspect, it only needs a whisper from someone seeking revenge for the district's harlots to spring into action.⁠
208938058:
Archerus Manor

Archerus Manor is the residence of one of the Inner Sea's most famous artists, the painter Endrik Archerus, who lives in a massive stone tower visible throughout the district.⁠
209539368:
Arcanamirium

The Arcanamirium is not only the largest and oldest school in Absalom, but quite possibly the most prestigious arcane magic academy in the entire Inner Sea region of Golarion.⁠⁠

224059448:
Cradle of Immortality

The Cradle of Immortality, located in the Tian Xia nation of Lingshen far to the north of the Golden River, is where artisans have sculpted terracotta likenesses of soldiers serving King Huang. His wizards have connected the statues to the souls of the warriors with the underworld dragon's blessing. Whenever one of these warriors dies, their soul is transferred to the terra-cotta soldier to continue serving their lord until the simulacrum is destroyed.⁠

The Cradle, which is a series of long structures arranged in a cluster, is surrounded by hundreds of clay quarries. Craftspeople sculpt the constructs from the clay inside of the Cradle, all similar in general shape, form, and equipment, and are arranged into groups for various ancestries.⁠

None has witnessed the harvesting of these souls on battlefields, and the process of collecting them and animating the soldiers is unknown not only to the public but also to all who work in the Cradle except its most senior laborers.⁠ The necromancer Laochong, the "Old Worm" as nicknamed by King Huang, is responsible for the soul-binding magic and uses the pricked blood collected when each soldier swears their oath to the crown. Not even King Huang knows Laochong's true nature or identity.⁠

A large cavern beneath the Cradle serves as a repository for souls to be installed into the terra-cotta forms.⁠ Record keepers track the souls, including the few that silently but knowingly go unaccounted for.⁠
224474888:
Ollo

The town of Ollo is one of the largest settlements in the Shackles. It is ruled by the cruel pirate Avimar Sorrinash, a member of the Pirate Council.

Ollo is on Shark Island and is plagued by raids from the sedacthies who live in the sea near the island. These raids are carried out with Sorrinash's permission, and the people of Ollo live in daily fear of a sedacthy attack.⁠
225023518:
Braughleigh's Hollow

Braughleigh's Hollow is something of an open, yet monstrous, secret amongst the people of the Avin Prefecture for it is an ogre settlement. Nestled in the foothills of the Fog Peaks, far from any road or other settlements, this secret group of ogres is the remnants of a much larger population that once ravaged the Avin Prefecture. Now, however, they restrict their raiding to the foothills of the Fog Peaks. Braughleigh's Hollow serves as a meeting place for the other monstrous tribes of the Fog Peaks, many of whom engage in human slavery.⁠

Rumour suggests nobles from Yanmass and even as far afield as the Northern Tandak Prefecture secretly visit Braughleigh's Hollow to acquire human chattel or quietly dispose of unwanted enemies or criminals. This foul trade is something of an open secret, but as long as the ogres stick to the mountains the Taldan authorities have proven willing to look the other way.⁠
225220568:
Garizés City

Sitting in the north-western reaches of the Arcadian nation of Xopatl, Garizés City is renowned for the prominent musical style that is named after it. This musical style is a lively one typified by an inclusion of common instruments, like flutes, guitars and trumpets, alongside the more unusual garizan, a musical instrument made of entwined plant matter that is squeezed and stretched to make different sounds. Garizés City is the primary place that garizans are manufactured and those that are not made in Garizés City are normally viewed as being of inherently inferior quality.⁠
228851428:
Eagle Garrison Fort

The Eagle Garrison Fort is a fortress of the Eagle Garrison located in the northern Kortos Mounts foothills, about 100 miles' travel from Diobel on land by way of Meravon.⁠
230326508:
Crystalhurst

Crystalhurst is a secretive town in the Southern Fangwood ruled by a circle of druids who make sure the homes and other structures of the town blend in with the natural landscape. The druids willingly help the Nirmathi repel Molthuni invaders,⁠⁠ now that their previous central concern, the fight against the Darkblight, was ended with the fall of the debased fey ruler Arlantia in 4717 AR.⁠
237251988:
Hinji

Hinji is a Chelaxian port city in the Archduchy of Longmarch, located on the Inner Sea west of Longmast Cape and east of Macini.⁠⁠
242578638:
Halfling Coast

The Halfling Coast is part of the southern shoreline of the largest of the Rampore Isles in the Shackles. The cruel rakshasa Bedu Hanji, who rules the Rampore Isles, has maliciously named it "Halfling Coast" because he used to crucify captured sailors from Bag Island ships there.⁠
258532158:
Farnvale

Farnvale is an isolated town with a dark secret, located deep in Galt's Boarwood, where the infamous Gray Gardeners never visited.⁠
269476118:
Jorgenfist

Jorgenfist is a fortress in the center Varisia's Iron Peaks, near the Muschkal River within the Valley of the Black Tower. Its walls incorporate the Black Tower on its southeastern side.⁠⁠
286366808:
Viritash's Tail

Viritash's Tail is an unholy valley within the section of the Pardaparbat Mountains inside the Narhari Desert. It is named after the evil Vudran dragon deity Viritash, and a scepter of incredible potency made from Viritash's severed tail remains at the heart of the valleys. The land surrounding Viritash's Tail is filled with numerous linnorms and other corrupt dragons fighting to claim the scepter for themselves.⁠
296714488:
Rumbutter

Rumbutter is the southernmost settlement on Bag Island in Shackles. It is a sprawling, hilly, farming community known for its apiaries and honey. Rumbutter honey finds its way throughout the Shackles and Sargava. Rumbutter's three taverns on its main road, Bedda's Berth, the Gilded Lily, and Shopin's Roundhouse, serve unique blends of iced butterscotch beers in the rainy season and honey wine in the drier months.⁠
298744228:
Mermaid's Bucket

The Mermaid's Bucket is a famous tavern located next to the main docks of Crescent Harbor in the pirate city of Port Peril. A rowdy bar, the Mermaid's Bucket is decorated with numerous depictions of merfolk, fish masks, and other nautical paraphernalia of all sorts, including an enormous mosaic of a mermaid behind the bar. The Mermaid's Bucket's proprietor Nefti Unwesha also supplies rum to every bar, tavern, and brothel in town, buying out her competition with strangely minted silver coins.⁠
311888088:
Maashinelle

Maashinelle is the largest settlement in Lambreth and serves as the seat of power for its dictator, Lord Kamdyn Arnefax. The town is located in the lowlands where the Tolemaida River joins the West Sellen River and has a large dockside along the water.⁠
315324828:
Dyinglight

Standing at the headwaters of the Sarkora River and surrounded by the marshes and sulfurous hotsprings of the Frostmire Fen, Dyinglight was once a major city in the Kellid nation of Sarkoris. Abandoned by its human inhabitants shortly after the opening of the Worldwound in 4606 AR, Dyinglight is now the home of a particularly violent band of fiendish, cannibalistic marsh giants.⁠⁠⁠
318881928:
Thorngate

Thorngate is a disabled⁠ elf gate near Tanglebriar in Kyonin.⁠ It was deactivated to prevent demons from corrupting it upon Treerazer's arrival and has remained inactive since then.⁠

Ropecliffs

Ropecliffs is a neighborhood where smugglers from the Precipice Quarter gather, having taken up the trade to survive the calamity that befell the district. 348907298:
Finder's Gulch

Finder's Gulch is a ruined and abandoned village in the Menador Mountains of western Isger that is home to a powerful priestess of Urgathoa named Illcayna Alonnor. She was transformed by her goddess into a monstrosity known as a daughter of Urgathoa and raids the countryside around Finder's Gulch—including neighboring Cheliax and Molthune—for victims to expand her growing army of wights.⁠
355855658:
Monastery of Tala

Located in central Mendev, the Monastery of Tala caters to many faiths of the crusaders going to fight the demons in the Worldwound.⁠ Run by a cloistered order of monks from numerous faiths named the Brotherhood of Tala, it was founded in 4702 AR as a place where the various churches could conduct research on how best to combat the demonic forces of the Worldwound.⁠
363896078:
Jangley's Shop

Jangley's Shop is a store run by the halfling brothers Pasker and Trill Jangley, who sell all sorts of curiosities. They use their extensive network of contacts to update their inventory daily, acquiring a wide variety of items at varying prices.⁠
386868458:
Thrushmoor

The settlement of Thrushmoor can be found in the Ustalavic county of Versex.⁠⁠ A fishing community on Lake Encarthan's Avalon Bay,⁠ the town is known to harbor a significant number of followers of the unsavory Old Cults,⁠ and the equally unsavoury Night Heralds.⁠
396250268:
Guiding Hand

The Guiding Hand is an establishment that offers food, shelter, and job opportunities in the poverty-stricken neighborhood of Mudhaven. Tern on the Wind is an elf from the Crown of the World who came to represent her insular people in the city, but upon witnessing the plight of the people in the streets, she began her religious mission to help the community. She follows Findeladlara, and the two-story building with stained-glass windows is kept clean thanks to magical wards amidst the filthy streets and buildings.⁠
397437418:
Oenopion

The Nexian city of Oenopion (pronounced oh-NOH-pee-ohn)⁠ is known as a center for alchemical production. Here they brew potions and elixirs which factor heavily in Nex's economy. The homunculi they create have a reputation for cunning and dependability, and the city also has a well-known golemworks. Within laboratories, mages and alchemists also work together in their perfection of the so-called art of fleshwarping.⁠

The central lake is the site of a massive ooze colony that has developed a hivemind.⁠ As well as being a useful means of disposing of unwanted items and people, the ooze has proved to be useful in divination magic.⁠

Oenopion is represented on Nex's ruling body, the Council of Three and Nine, by master alchemist Borume.⁠
398658318:
Sombrefell Hall

The massive manor known as Sombrefell Hall is located about 25 miles northeast of Rozenport in Ustalav. It is situated at the end of a fairly well demarcated road abutting the Lantern Lake. The manor has belonged to the Oscilar family for generations. It is built in the gothic Ustalavic fashion and its grand entrance consists of mahogany double doors.⁠
409315508:
Left-Handed Lobster

The Left-Handed Lobster is a bar open only to the fishermen members of Magnimar's Outcast Fishery. It is located within the Fishery's complex in the Beacon's Point district.⁠⁠
420935418:
Beragel's Fur and Feathers

Beragel's Fur and Feathers is a pet shop run by Beragel Tindertales, offering animals from all over Golarion, as well as food and specialized enclosures to keep them happy. As a rule, sentient animals, endangered species, and monsters are not sold in the shop, though, whether by mistake or due to her gnome tendencies for novelties, she sometimes acquires a larva or hatchling that later turns out to be something that shouldn't be anyone's pet.⁠
422770398:
Stepped Tower of Djedefar

The Stepped Tower of Djedefar is a site in northern Osirion. It is located on the north eastern tip of the Alamein Peninsula.⁠ The tower is home to a community of Irori-worshiping monks.⁠
423039718:
Tiven's Reed

Tiven's Reed is a small gnome settlement in central Katapesh, very similar to Yavipho. It is located near an oasis and began as a stopover for merchant caravans.⁠
427966818:
Osprey Club

The Osprey Club, located in the Naos district of Magnimar, caters to a restrictive clientele of the richest families in the city. Gambling, drinking, and smoking are common activities here; there is also a brothel, for those so inclined. The exterior of the club is guarded by an iron fence to keep the onlookers outside. Green and gold magical lights illuminate the outside every night. The club is currently run by Kayasi Zivatchi.⁠

Whitespectre Canyon

Whitespectre Canyon is a box canyon in the Nesmian Plains of Nirmathas. Numerous predators have claimed the canyon for themselves. As of 4717 AR it was plagued by Witchpelt, a giant smilodon that escaped from a traveling Varisian circus.⁠

Andos Hall

Andos Hall, the city hall of Kintargo, is located in its Castle District and thoroughly dwarfed by the neighbouring Castle Kintargo, next to which it appears understated and quaint.⁠

Adrast

The Barony of Adrast is a small barony and settlement in the north-west of Taldor, located north of the Verduran Forest and south of the westernmost mountains of the Fog Peaks in the Northern Tandak Prefecture.⁠⁠ The Baron of Adrast is Baron Stelan who is married to Baroness Lenelle. The headsman of Adrast settlement, a small village, is Odric, and the captain of the guard is the dromaar Captain Drelm. Following the baron's professed faith, the predominant religion is that of Abadar, and the barony has a cleric and temple to that god.⁠

Iadara

The illusion-shrouded city of Iadara (pronounced eye-uh-DAR-ah)⁠ is the beautiful capital of the elven kingdom of Kyonin.⁠
482805308:
Sunless Pond

After Earthfall, the Nidalese people faced crop challenges due to the lack of sunlight. Zon-Kuthon provided a solution: the Sunless Pond in the Uskwood. This supernatural spring feeds a pond whose dark water has plant growth-enhancing properties. Shades of the Uskwood druids distribute its water annually to peasants, collecting taxes for the water while assessing the arcane potential of local children. Despite the weak sun's return, farmers still rely on the pond's water to bolster crops for survival, attending gatherings for the precious resource despite the unpleasantness involved.⁠
500839868:
East Rikkan

The small port towns of East Rikkan and Westpool, located north of Westcrown in Cheliax, are known collectively as the Rikkan Ports. These settlements house large numbers of merchants who trade goods up and down the River Adivian, and as of 4709 AR (prior to the abolition of slavery in Cheliax) also housed the numerous slaves required to operate the Stavian Arches and portage stations. Although Westpool is larger, East Rikkan has more docks for fishermen and travelers.⁠
506996448:
Jexler & Young Salvage Company and Deep Sea Exploration and Retrieval

Jexler & Young Salvage Company and Deep Sea Exploration and Retrieval is located in a large warehouse along the docks of Katapesh and does exactly what its name suggests. Founded by the adventurous sailors Darg Jexler and Wilbur Young, nowadays they limit themselves to wreck salvaging and tourist tours,⁠ they also sell items useful to adventurers heading to aquatic environments. Whenever news reaches Katapesh of a wrecked ship or nearby sunken treasure Jexler and Young are normally the first to investigate. Their ship the Iron Mermaid is specially designed for salvage operations and is a common sight in the water around the city. Currently word has reached them of a new opportunity, the Star Runner was attacked relatively nearby by a huge sea monster suspected to be a kraken. Supposedly the cargo holds of the Star Runner were stuffed to the brim with trade goods and ancient relics from the Mwangi Expanse.⁠ Jexler & Young are desperate to get there before the expedition from Annexa Palanthea's Fishy Menagerie who are after the sea monster but are none the less rivals.⁠
509371468:
Crystalcrag

Crystalcrag is a town of geniekin in the remote southern Zho Mountains of Qadira. Due to prejudices against geniekin, the town is protected by illusions created by Tygora Cinderfury, an ifrit exile from Medina Mudii'a.⁠⁠
509616628:
Wait's Span

Wait's Span is the name of a tiny hamlet next to a wooden bridge of the same name that sits near the southeastern shore of Lake Kavapesta in the Ustalavic province of Ulcazar. It is located only six miles east of the Monastery of the Veil, and was the site of a massive fire that destroyed most of the village. Although Bishop Senir of the Monastery claims this was a natural event, most locals believe otherwise.⁠

The Wait's Span has since also been referred to as the Senir Bridge and it is noted as being quite a large bridge. Here ancient stones mark the border between the mountain county of Ulcazar and the vales of Amaans. Gargoyles, their faces worn by time, decorate the sides of the high arches of the bridge. It has not been well maintained and it has large crumbling gaps along its length at various places.⁠
514555698:
Blackwood Moot

Blackwood Moot is an isolated stand of Blackwood trees deep in the Verduran Forest of Taldor that serves as a meeting place for wild residents dissatisfied with the Treaty of the Wildwood. Those who meet at Blackwood Moot view the members of the Wildwood Lodge as traitors who have enabled Taldor's destruction of the Verduran Forest.⁠

The Blackwood Moot is led by the arboreal regent Oakadence, a powerful sorcerer who has been organising secretive raids on Wispil and the Isle of Arenway using the wild beasts of the forest as disposable foot soldiers.⁠
515747788:
Forgotten Track

The Forgotten Track is a prison mine located at the bottom of a large canyon in a region of Razmiran known as the Tracks. Those who have lost faith in or displease the Church of Razmir are sent here; it is called the Forgotten Track because that is the eventual fate of most who are sent there.⁠
544124728:
Century Root

The Century Root is a massive, half-mile-wide tree stump located in the southern Fierani Forest of Kyonin, just south and east of a bend in the Kyonin River. As of 4709 AR it was the location of a arboreal regent moot, a meeting of these woodland protectors from across the forest.⁠
546688808:
Grand Dance Hall of Kortos

The Grand Dance Hall of Kortos is an ornate, round theater on the district of The Coins in the city of Absalom.

The city's richest merchants and most ambitious nobles gather in the theater to organise deals in order to control the economy of the Inner Sea. Admission is free to those in the appropriate attire, but access to the hall's three balconies requires increasingly audacious fees as the guest ascends the levels.

The entertainment includes the finest Vudrani dancers and gymnasts from throughout the Inner Sea and beyond.⁠
548152998:
Khopesh Span

The Khopesh Span is a large stone bridge that crosses the Crook River in southern Osirion. It was built during the height of Osirian power in -2370 AR, and besides the shallows at the city of Ipeq, provides the only other place to safely cross the river. It is still operational to this day and is a part of the overland trade route between Osirion and its southern neighbor, Katapesh.⁠
560963288:
Vira Oberigo

Located in the Rego Corna sector of Westcrown, Vira Oberigo has been the historic residence of House Oberigo since the Four Families Siege. The family controlled most of the activities that took place on the island of Siraon.⁠

645655198:
Uldani Necropolis

The Uldani Necropolis is a site in the desert interior of Thuvia. It lies not far from the city of Pashow.⁠
647386118:
House of Healing

The House of Healing is a Sarenite temple in the Ivy District in Absalom. It offers healing free of charge to any who need it and works to help former slaves in the city.⁠ As of 4720 AR, Zharichela was the House's high priestess.⁠
651506458:
Clover's Crossing

Clover's Crossing was a thriving village in the north of the Ustalavic province of Canterwall until it was overrun by a large numbers of ghouls who rose up out the local church's graveyard. As of 4711 AR, Clover's Crossing was a ghost town that few willingly agree to enter.⁠
661836458:
Palace of the Child-Goddess

The Palace of the Child-Goddess is a flat-topped pyramid in the Ankar-Te ring district of Kaer Maga. It is the home of at least one child-goddess, who is worshiped as a living deity within the city. Its single, massive door is the only way in and out. From there, windowless, metal palanquins allegedly bearing the child-goddess are carried through the streets multiple times a day, where the faithful believe her presence wards them from evil and danger. Whether the child-goddesses are actually carried within is not definitively known, as the metal palanquins have no windows and most members of the Cult of the Child-Goddess do not talk to outsiders.

The Palace is overseen by the High Priestess Shamalay Kasan, the only of the child-goddess's clergy who regularly interacts with the city's general populace.⁠
671052938:
Vira Julistarc

Vira Julistarc is a group of structures under the same crystalline roof on the island of Dlaratha, in Rego Corna in Westcrown. Its form is based upon a Taldan defensive tradition maintained by House Julistarc, in addition to more modern advancements in defensive architecture.⁠
685033738:
Rivenstone

Rivenstone is a submerged mountain within the Broken Bay region of the Lands of the Linnorm Kings that causes great trouble to passing ships. Rivenstone rises up from the depth of one of the deepest valleys of the Steaming Sea, splitting on its way up into seven separate peaks. The highest two peaks reach just below the sea's surface except at the lowest tides when they poke above the tideline; they are known to local sailors but seem to have a knack for sinking visiting ships. Another danger is the presence of a Dagon-worshipping tribe of intelligent gutaki devilfish. They are led by a cabal of a dozen priests, a mix of clerics and oracles, who use charmed giant octopuses and squid to bolster their tribe making them one of the deadliest threats to dwell within Broken Bay.⁠⁠

700375678:
Tomb of the Living

The Tomb of the Living is located in Westgate and is built in the Osirian style. Thanks to the loophole that those who continue to move when entombed can be imprisoned without trial after being buried, the city maintains that this is a tomb, not a prison and its spaciousness allows them to incarcerate enemies of the city indefinitely, whenever they wish, without technically breaking the laws established by Aroden. The prison's existence is a secret from the masses and other nations, who would not react well to its presence. The city performs rituals in the upper crypts, which contain the corpses of nobles who lacked the means for burial elsewhere in the city and below lies a labyrinth of cells accessible only to members of the Sally Guard, those who reveal its secret are punished by being imprisoned in the tomb. The darkness, scarce food and water, and limited space drive those imprisoned here insane, causing their muscles to atrophy and constantly weakened.⁠

Some of the prisoners here whose names have been forgotten include:

  • The Almost Goddess, around 4700 AR, a charismatic woman who arrived in Absalom to take the Test of the Starstone. She amassed a large following and was talented in everything she did; no one doubted she would become a goddess. On the day she was to take the test, she disappeared and was forgotten.
  • The Forever Wizard, a researcher obsessed with his own mortality, tried to overcome it, and surprisingly, contrary to what usually happens with these immortality schemes, he achieved eternal life. After experimenting on his own body, he achieved perfect regeneration, making it impossible for him to die from violence or old age. He was going to leave to go see his elderly parents in Taldor to share the secret of immortality with them and then with the rest of the world. He disappeared the day before he was to leave by ship.
  • The Quiet King, a nobleman of the city, witnessed all the atrocities Absalom committed for the "good of the nation", and his conscience wouldn't allow him to let this continue. He spoke to journalists, telling them he would bring them proof of these atrocities and that they should wait for him. Now he is in a cell under constant magical silence, and his tongue has been cut out.⁠
708109118:
Iron Mountain

The Iron Mountain is located in the Wall of Heaven range of Tian Xia south of Quain. A platform guarded by sentinel statues of foo lions was built long ago near one of the peaks of the Iron Mountain. This platform contains twin gates: one leading to Heaven, and the other to Hell. Once every 12 years, the imperial dragon known in Quain as the Celestial Dragon visits the site and grants one wish to a royal maiden.⁠
722287208:
Wrathwarped Halls

The Wrathwarped Halls were a Bakrakhan research complex beneath the Calphiak Mountains, dedicated to the study and creation of new weapons and soldiers for use in the wars against Shalast. In the modern era, it was forgotten until goblins from the Rocksmashers tribe discovered the site while rolling their iconic boulder totem. The goblins seized the site, using its laboratories to enhance their capabilities, and began plotting their conquest of the other tribes in the area.⁠ Shoantis discovered the location in 4717 AR and requested the Pathfinder Society's assistance in investigating the ruins.⁠ The energies of fury were sealed away by a priest from Soralyon who had heard about the ruins.⁠
725676378:
Halgrim

The city of Halgrim is the second largest settlement in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings; only Kalsgard is bigger. Located on the northwestern shore of Battlewall, one of the largest islands in the Ironbound Archipelago, Halgrim was founded by King Igarven in 2655 AR.⁠ Today, it is ruled by the Linnorm King White Estrid from her palace. The Rustflow River flows out to the sea through Halgrim and, famously, seven bridges cross the river within the city. The city's defenses are greatly enhanced by the constant presence of White Astrid's linnorm thrall, Boiltongue.⁠⁠⁠⁠
726822268:
Shouk

The Shouk is a tribe of degenerate ogrekin that once were human holy men. Their lair is in the Barrier Wall mountains, roughly south-east of the Thuvian city of Duwwor.⁠ Once the Shouk were holy men and oracles of some renown. Their wisdom was sought by many other nomadic tribes. However, at some point in the distant past, this clan of holy men became tainted by the blood of ogres and ogrekin began to be born among the ranks of the Shouk. With each generation the taint spread, and more and more brutish, vile ogrekin were born. Now the tribe is composed exclusively of ogrekin, and has lost all prophetic ability. Purely out of tradition, the tribes of the area still occasionally seek out the Shouk in times of great need. These visits rarely yield any result other than the loss of life, as the Shouk are also now cannibals.⁠

Maheto

Maheto is a highly-defended Taldan city located in the northern foothills of the World's Edge Mountains. This settlement is home to highly-skilled dwarven craftsmen whose blades and other products are in high demand by members of the empire's ruling class.⁠⁠⁠

As a symbol of their allegiance to Taldor the legendary sword Turlang was forged and given to Grand Prince Arthune. This blade commiserates the slaying of an ancient dragon named Tharularg and is a masterpiece of Dwarven craftsmanship.⁠
755551108:
Wedding rock

Wedding rock is a ruined ancient Azlanti altar on the island of Nal-Kashel, in the Hellmouth Gulf west of Cheliax. Residents of Blackcove, a village on the gulf's coast, traditionally consummate their marriage vows on the altar.⁠
761707418:
Coldwater

Coldwater is a small town on the western bank of the Gullik River in the Irriseni capital province of Thronehold. Baroness Wilimina is the ruler of the town.⁠

The peasants of Coldwater look with envy the changing seasons in the Realm of the Mammoth Lords but no peasant is allowed to cross the river. They have to work the docks and house and entertain the merchants traveling up and down the Gullik River. Some young and rebellious Jadwiga have formed a stilyagi gang and call themselves the Lords of the Tusk. They are led by Paval Turosky, a foolish youth, and enjoy crossing the river and imitate the Kellid barbarians. On some occasions the Lords wander deep into the foreign lands and they say they want to forage deeper into the wilds to hunt bison and the prehistoric animals that roam those lands.⁠
771696698:
Lyperro

Lyperro is a small village in the Rhuzam region of Druma.⁠

Highdelve

Nadzieja Lato

830912938:
Shoreline Road

Shoreline Road is a road that crosses Greengold and continues along the shore of Lake Encarthan to reach Druma in the southeast.⁠
838450728:
Hessim, Newby, and Sage Paint Manufactory

Hessim, Newby, and Sage Paint Manufactory is an art supplies shop with a sagging store front that sits in the Old Korvosa district of Korvosa. The store, which was founded in 4600 AR,⁠ is filled with art supplies, canvases, easels, pots, and brushes. The paints from Hessim, Newby, and Sage Paint Manufactory vary from the cheapest, a one silver piece white paint, all the way up to a dazzling shade of violet—Newby Violet—that costs forty gold pieces a jar. Regardless of price, their paints are renowned as being the best in all Korvosa for colour, consistency, and permanence. The owners of the shop, Hessim, Newby, and Sage, are a trio of very old men who all wear glasses and are very ingratiating towards their customers.⁠
838970438:
Painted Flutes

The Painted Flutes is a vast canyon nestled within the Barrier Wall mountains of western Katapesh. The valley is named for the unique geological phenomena found within, including dozens of hoodoos—tall, wind carved pillars of rock that look like totem poles—that are made of a variety of layers of different, brightly-coloured rocks as a spectacular landscape. The wind howls through the valley and when it reaches the right speed in creates haunting music like some sort of giant wind instrument.

Due to the forces of erosion constantly changing its shape, as well as its strong winds, the direction and duration the song created by the hoodoos is never the same twice. The valley attracts many bards and other musicians to hear its wondrous song. The valley is also inhabited by clans of janns and wandering air elementals who roam the deep canyons.⁠⁠
839749298:
Bolgrad

Bolgrad is an underground mining city in the northeastern Five Kings Range that specializes in gemstones; the cavern city's gem-rich ceiling earned it the nickname "Star-Studded Bolgrad". Most of its majority dwarven population works either in the mining and processing of gems or as jewelers.⁠
863128668:
Kalsgard

The city of Kalsgard is located on the southern banks of the Rimeflow River in the northern reaches of the Lands of the Linnorm Kings known as the Thanelands. It is the largest city in the Lands of the Linnorm Kings, and as such is the most cosmopolitan city for several hundred miles, housing communities of dwarves, gnomes, Varisians, and people from even further afield.⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠
864563458:
Algidheart

The city of Algidheart is the regional capital of the Irrisen province of Bleakmarch. It lies to the west of Glacier Lake on the Rimeflow River. From the city, the Rimeflow continues westward into the Lands of the Linnorm Kings.⁠⁠⁠ The city's buildings are built upon bridges across the river, and rise to staggering heights. They are connected by a tangled network of platforms, ladders, and ramps.⁠
867600338:
Fort Thorn

Fort Thorn a small settlement with a stone keep beset by feral fey, owlbears, flame drakes, lizardfolk, bugbears, and other threats in the Bloodsworn Vale.⁠ Around 4707 AR, then-King of Korvosa Eodred Arabasti II appointed Sir Gyrad Tolgrith to establish Fort Thorn and a trade route through the vale.⁠
870018998:
Street of Sighs

The Street of Sighs is located in the Oriat district, which is full of three-story apartment buildings where most of the Sweettalkers live. Because their mouths are sealed shut, they communicate through noises, which give the street its name, and this "silent" community can be seen going about their daily lives like any other here.⁠
878193918:
Guild of Wonders

The headquarters of the Guild of Wonders is ostensibly an unmarked, poorly received tourism attraction composed of creative taxidermy that purportedly depicts cryptids and other beings, and is located in a shoddy building in the Westgate neighborhood of Absalom. However, its decrepit appearance masks its true purpose as a guildhouse for assassins, spies, and saboteurs.⁠
890997878:
Cayden's Hall


Cayden's Hall in the Ascendant Court district of Absalom is a large, boisterous meadhall and temple of Cayden Cailean, built of wood as was the original meadhall from which Cayden set out to take the Test of the Starstone.⁠ Due to the drunken revelry, religious bonfires, and consequent accidents, this is the fourteenth temple built on the current site near a large fountain, which is itself at least the fourth site to house Cayden's temple.⁠

Efforts are made by the local priests and the house guards to quell any serious fights and extinguish uncontrolled fires, despite the fact that they are often as inebriated as the patrons who frequent the hall. Aside from simple drinks and food, the hall also boasts a mid-sized speaking hall, intended for both religious proclamations and general entertainment.⁠

Ruled by High Priestess Saphira, the Lady of Intemperance, it is not merely a place to get drunk, but also a gathering-hall for adventurers to meet and plot expeditions, rebellions, and exploits of all kinds.⁠
894678438:
Consulate of the Platinum Band

The Consulate of the Platinum Band is a temple dedicated to Apsu where his non-draconic followers gather and help others. Although the faith isn't widely understood by the residents of The Puddles, they won't refuse the magical assistance offered. The building also houses archives on the region's dragon lore. The Consulate has few members, distinguished by their pendants bearing the symbol of their god. The rest avoid leaving the temple and do not interact with the Muckruckers or other ruthless groups in the district.⁠
897371598:
Skywatch

The abandoned city of Skywatch is built around a massive observatory high in the Icerime Peaks on Brevoy's eastern border. Once a holding of House Surtova, it was mysteriously sealed for 20 years before being reopened and revealed to be abandoned in 4722 AR.⁠⁠
907429048:
Torch

Torch is an unusual town in central Numeria that sits in a crescent around a bizarre, black hillock of shiny black stone known as Torch Hill. Atop the hill is the town's namesake, a brilliant purple bonfire that occasionally explodes into a devastating miles-high pillar of flame.⁠
912585518:
Kennel

The Kennel appears to be an unremarkable taxidermy shop, in a state of disrepair similar to other buildings in the district, but it's used by the Family Dogs criminal gang, named for all the taxidermied dogs found in the establishment's basement.⁠ The members have moved the dogs around, posing them as if they were people, which has increased the shop's reputation. Although none of the members yet know how to taxidermy, some are trying to learn. The leader, Dras, keeps the "pack" in line, and some of his members want to expand their activities into racketeering. They've already demonstrated what happens to those who don't pay, sealing their mouths shut and creating a legend about a monster that can only be scared away by taxidermied figurines.⁠

Embassy of New Thassilon

The Embassy of New Thassilon, located in the Foreign Quarter, represents the interests of Eurythnia and Edasseril in Absalom. These factors deal not only in their own currency, but also in information, alliances, and veiled threats. Many adventurers come to the Grand Exchange looking for sponsorship to explore Golarion's hidden corners.⁠

Witchcaves

The Witchcaves are a series of deep caverns in the south eastern region of Irrisen's Hoarwood province. According to legend, great power lies in these caves, which are also suspected of having an entrance to the Darklands.

In 3937 AR the survivors of the failed Harcatha Rebellion fled to the caves in the hope of recruiting Darklands allies to help their cause. Nothing more was heard of them until 4079 AR, when an insane force of Jadwiga emerged from the caves and rampaged across the region until they were wiped out by Irriseni forces led by General Chernim Karina.

Queen Karina, Irrisen's then ruler, ordered the caves sealed. However, a few adventurers recently defied the ban and investigated the caves—and found them overrun by qlippoth. Because they were preoccupied with the war, the hole was never excavated, nor were the bodies recovered, and rumors of vengeful spirits keep people away from the site. The area inside the sinkhole overlooks a hryngar settlement that was abandoned when the local ore ran out, though recently a group of prospectors, led by a hryngar named Asdynn the Breaker, has been attempting to reclaim the citadel. Because many monsters from the Darklands have claimed parts of the citadel, clearing it will take a considerable amount of time.⁠⁠
1109409378:

Saventh-Yhi

The ruined city of Saventh-Yhi (pronounced saa-vinth-YHEE) is located in the southern Mwangi Jungle, east of the Ocota River, just north of the Bandu Hills.⁠ The city was founded more than 10,000 years ago during the Age of Legend by followers of the Azlanti hero Savith, who died while defeating the serpentfolk god Ydersius in the Darklands' tunnels below.⁠
1185159038:
Etran's Folly

Etran's Folly, originally named Etranton, and also known as Plaguestone, is a tiny Isgeri town that has seen better days.⁠

Meeting Post

The Meeting Post is a monument of presumed shoanti origin used as a meeting place by friends and merchants. The totem pole rises above the surrounding shops, and the animals it depicts have amorphous proportions, making them seem more alien than normal. Mercenaries seeking to offer their services in exchange for money leave notes on the totem pole with ways to contact them.⁠
1197512588:
Nicyruse

Nicyruse was an ancient city of the Jistka Imperium located today in southern Avistan, on the Inner Sea coast. It housed one of the largest temple-forges in all the Imperium, rivaling even that of Rachikan. When Jistka's doom became imminent, divine earthquakes tore the region apart and city's forges were abandoned. Now the seaside ruins of Nicyruse have mostly eroded away by the Inner Sea.⁠

In 4712 AR, reports from the Chelaxian city of Hinji to the east stated that a recent storm had cleared a new entrance to the buried site. Fisherfolk said that mechanical creatures began moving across the shore near the ruins, grabbing fish from the ocean with their bare hands, and taking them back into the ruins. The Pathfinder Society has called for adventurers to explore the ruins and bring back any information about lost Jistka.⁠
1200143568:
Ysborg

Ysborg is located just below the snowline on the northern slopes of Mount Gnarlfang, in the western Kodar Mountains at the far south-eastern corner of the Linnorm Kingdom of Southmoor, where borders provide no real barrier to the eternal winter of neighboring Irrisen.⁠

Ysborg, the "Steading of the Ice Trolls", is something between a town and a fortress, consisting of crude wooden buildings and hide tents, all sized for giant occupants, surrounded by a stout wooden palisade. The entire fortress is surrounded by a moat of nearly freezing water inhabited by numerous river drakes.⁠

Frost trolls, ettins, ogres, and other giants come from all across the Linnorm Kingdoms to join the army of the Blue Jarl, a huge powerfully muscled frost troll with a giant battleaxe curved from magical ice.⁠

The streets of Ysborg are dangerous, with brutal fights and fresh blood on the snow to be a common sight. The Blue Jarl's "Winter Palace" is one of Ysborg's few stone buildings. It is nothing more than a blocky pile of icy rocks but it is well-fortified. The throne of the Blue Jarl is made from carved mammoth tusks and is decorated with human skulls. The Blue Jarl's kennels, just outside the palace are filled with winter wolves who have sworn allegiance to the jarl and the Bear Pits host ferocious polar and grizzly bears armored and trained to fight.⁠

The Blue Jarl is always accompanied by his loyal frost giant shield maidens, as well as by the huge, white-furred dire bear that serves as his mount.⁠

Frost troll marauders from Ysborg frequently raid neighboring human settlements for slaves, or more often, fresh food, for frost trolls relish the taste of human flesh. The villages have appealed to Trollheim for aid but for now usually defend themselves or abandon their villages. Rumors hold that Irrisen has been courting Ysborg as an ally, but so far, the trolls remain independent.⁠⁠

Jernashall became the preeminent city of the new empire, although Highhelm remained its capital. Jernashall became so important that the nations of Cheliax and Isger petitioned it to help them build a surface city close to it. Tomb of the First Battle

A dirt path branching off from Deepgate leads to a cavern filled with warnings that no orc should proceed further. Inside, the giants rest, protected by Ogon, one of the warriors who survived that fierce battle.⁠

As a result, in addition to an inn, stable, and general store, it also boasts a surprisingly large cathedral. However, the mineral deposits were eventually exhausted, and the death of Aroden led to the cathedral being closed down and boarded up. Most of the population soon relocated to Kalabuto,⁠ and Stark Point become little more than a general store.⁠

The abandoned cathedral might be haunted, and some have claimed to have seen strange lights and heard chanting coming from within.⁠

1373934458:
Oagon

Oagon was a city in the now-lost kingdom of Lirgen. Its location at the mouth of the Black Flow river (in what is now known as the Sodden Lands) ensured it was completely covered by floodwater on the advent of the Eye of Abendego in 4606 AR.⁠
1376505868:
Avilan

Avilan is one of the numerous massive trading cities that dot the Qadiran region of the Plains of Paresh, but is often overshadowed by the capital of Katheer. It is located along the northern banks of the Pashman River halfway between Demirah and the capital, Katheer.⁠⁠

Redleaf

The settlement of Redleaf is located in the western portion of the Ustalavic county of Varno, circling the small Lake Redleaf.⁠⁠⁠⁠
1385155768:
Cyphergate

The Cyphergate is a cyclopean stone arch, straddling the entrance to Riddleport's harbor to a height of over 350 feet. Because its height is exactly half of the arch's width, it is believed by many that the arch is but one half of a larger ring, the second half of which is buried within the rocks and silt of the harbor bottom.⁠ The origins of the Cyphergate are widely thought to be Thassilonian, as the monument is built from unrecognizable stone and is decorated with mysterious runes, similar to other magically preserved carvings throughout the Varisian countryside.⁠ These runes are a topic for debate among scholars, both in the City of Cyphers and beyond. Some scholars believe they have no meaning, as they resist even magical detection methods, while others have formed a group called the Order of Cyphers and call themselves Cyphermages, dedicating their lives to uncovering the truth behind the enigmatic symbols.⁠⁠

1396052488:
Viridian Nexus

Corazal can share their knowledge with those they deems worthy by showing a repository of events that occurred in the forest.⁠

Nybor

Nybor, founded in 4641 AR,⁠ is perhaps the most racially accepting settlement in Varisia and ranks highly among the list in all of Golarion.⁠ Located on the southern shores of Ember Lake and bordering the Sanos Forest,⁠ the peaceful farming community has a more half-breeds per capita than any other Varisian city. Interracial marriages are not only tolerated, but promoted, making it a haven for those who find themselves in precarious situations involving illicit pregnancies and other affairs which might be judged harshly in more puritanical locations.⁠ Being so close to the Sanos Forest, Nybor is also home to a sizeable gnome population.⁠
1500011128:
House of Shade and Grace

The House of Shade and Grace is a popular Thuvian-style inn in the Foreign Quarter of the city. Built of sun-dried brick, it serves food that evokes memories of home for its guests. As one might expect, thuvians in the city, such as Lord Yamthar, are heavily involved with the establishment, lending their clockworks to assist with the service.⁠
1507932988:
Seven Stelae

The Seven Stelae is a collection of massive pillars located between Shiman-Sekh and the port city of Totra in Osirion. The red granite pillars bear the symbols of Pharaoh An-Hepsu I. Several doors and chambers in the pillars have been found.⁠

Port Peril

1523232608:
Finderplain

Near the center of Katapesh, the small gnome town of Finderplain provides temporary home for travelers exploring the area.⁠

Finderplain has stood 300 years as a way-point for gnomes traveling south of the Inner Sea.⁠ It holds almost 2,000 residents, but the constant influx and departure means that the number could change completely every few years. Families rarely establish permanent homes in Finderplain; the lure of adventure and desert beckons, and the gnomes move on, leaving their houses empty for the next travelers. The transitory nature of the gnomes means that no individual consistently rules over Finderplain. The current ruler is a gnome bard named Wexlis Bean.⁠
1545103498:
Erastil Club

The Erastil Club is the largest hunting lodge in Absalom, boasting an altar where its select members offer a prayer to the god of the hunt before leaving the city in pursuit of their prey. For a fee, anyone can become a member, but they must prove their hunting skills to advance in the ranks. Those who kill wolves or stags are permitted in the lounge, lions in the wine cellar, and bulettes or gorgons can sleep in the living quarters. If they confirm the death of a dragon that has claimed the lives of innocents, the member receives a medal and a pension for the hunt. The Board is composed of Lord Avid, Lord Celedo, and Asilia of Gyr, who ensure that animals are not overhunted and that all hunts are confirmed as legitimate.⁠
1574560868:
Fort Ozem

Fort Ozem is a Chernasardo Rangers fortress in Southern Fangwood. Fort Ozem was once used as a staging post in the war against the Whispering Tyrant. It is said that the fort was briefly home to Iomedae herself. The Rangers use it as a hideout. The worn outer walls are overgrown with vegetation. Its appearance has been deliberately neglected to indicate that there is nothing inside worth investigating. If enemies ever do draw near, the fort can be evacuated at a moment's notice.⁠⁠
1580722358:
Caldamin

Caldamin is a small, rural town in northernmost Andoran, nestled between the Five Kings Mountains to the west, the Verduran Forest to the east, and the Dragonfly River to the south.⁠ This otherwise unremarkable settlement has become somewhat of a tourist attraction of late, due to the presence of two extraordinary creatures who make their home nearby: a red reaver named Auger and a gray render called Shepherd Graygulp. These two foes occasionally battle each other, and their fights are of such ferocity that people come from far afield to witness the clashes.⁠
1602456418:
Winter Grove

The Winter Grove is an ancient druid's grove that lies within the Barrowood in Cheliax. Ruined and blackened, the grove predates the old empire of Taldor, before the rise of Cheliax as an independent nation.

Rumours say that within the grove lies a summoning circle of ancient origin, and that within this circle Abrogail I made her dark dealings with Asmodeus. In recent times, locals to the region have witnessed members of the royal family making regular (but secretive) visits to the site, always bringing sacrificial victims with them.⁠
1606832568:
Razorhall

Razorhall is a temple dedicated to the murderous aspect of Norgorber known as Father Skinsaw. The building, the former district courthouse, lies amidst the flooded houses of The Puddles. The cultists now hold sham trials where the accused are always found guilty and subjected to gruesome and creative executions. The courtroom tables and walls are covered in blood and skins of unknown origin. The murders have intensified recently, and the Muckruckers are too afraid of the cult to act against them, at least as long as they don't bother other important members of the district.⁠
1616049568:
Orolo's Quay

Orolo's Quay is a nearly forgotten seaside town on Nidal's Conqueror's Bay.

Before the founding of the Varisian city-states of Korvosa and Magnimar, it was the last port before the long voyage through the wilderness to the cities of the Lands of the Linnorm Kings. These days, the town and its Chelaxian fortress dating back to the Everwar have fallen into stark neglect, as very few ships dock here anymore. The only ships who make anchor at the crumbling wharf are those either desperate for supplies, or are smugglers bringing goods into Nidal who wish to avoid the harsh authorities in Nisroch farther south.

The first floor of the fortress has been converted into a shabby inn and trading post, with an attached stable of little note. Recently, rumors have begun to circulate that smugglers pay handsomely to store contraband in the fortress' old dungeons.⁠
1624229138:
Labyrinth of the Two Hells

The Labyrinth of the Two Hells is an extensive series of caves under the northern Zi Ha mountains that is home to two tribes of fiendish xulgaths.⁠ The Gugrangmyal are the "children of the cold hell" while the Gutshadmyal are the "children of the hot hell", and both equally brutal groups are in a perpetual war against the other.⁠⁠ The war, nurtured by the samsaran Baijan who manipulated the xulgaths' spiritual personas, has persisted for centuries.⁠
1626290128:
Monastery of the Unremitting Tide

The Monastery of the Unremitting Tide is historically an Iroran monastery on the eastern coast of Nex.⁠
1631067958:
Steelhead Pier

The Steelhead Pier is always bustling with people embarking or disembarking, making it the most busy pier in all of Greengold. It's traditional to name piers after freshwater fish, and the Steelhead's and the other piers share similar names.⁠
1658814808:
Wachail Estate
